draft.title: International action on biodiversity
card: Species and ecosystems cross borders, and no single country can protect them alone. International agreements are deals between countries that set shared goals and rules.
The Convention on Biological Diversity aims to conserve biodiversity, use it sustainably and share its benefits fairly. Countries that join agree to make national plans to meet these aims.

The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species controls the trade in listed animals and plants. Countries use permits to limit or ban trade in species that trade could push towards extinction.
These agreements rely on each country to act. They coordinate action between countries, but a country that does not follow the rules can still harm species.
draft.remember: Agreements coordinate countries: the CBD sets broad aims, and CITES controls trade in listed species.

a.q: Why are international agreements used to protect biodiversity?
opts: Species cross borders, so countries need shared action
Each country controls the species in other countries
Species live in one country only, so rules must match
Agreements remove the need for national plans
a.why: Species and ecosystems cross borders, so countries must coordinate their action. The last option is wrong because countries that join the CBD still make national plans.
a.clue: Think about what animals and ecosystems do at borders.

b.q: A trader in Country X tries to export a rare parrot listed under CITES. Which action fits how CITES works?
opts: Country X requires a permit before the parrot is exported
Country X must write a plan to restore the parrot's habitat
Country X must share the parrot's profits with other countries
Country X is forced by CITES to stop all trade in birds
b.why: CITES controls trade in listed species through permits, so an export needs a permit. Writing national plans to conserve biodiversity is the broad aim of the CBD, not the trade control of CITES. CITES does not ban all trade in birds, only controls trade in listed species.
b.clue: Which agreement deals with trade in listed species?
